answer: Timing-correlation clustering flags fake identities run by one operator. Each epoch the network logs when every account submits and which answers it grades, then merges accounts whose submission-time gaps and grade choices correlate above 0.9 across 10 epochs. A merged cluster earns one reward share, like a single vault paying out once. Every extra fake on the same island of hardware adds nothing, while avoiding the merge needs separate hosts and jittered schedules per fake, so cost grows with each identity. A lagoon of quiet clones is still caught by its correlation.
